Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We propose a substantial resolution that delivers direct payments to all identifiable members without a claims barrier. The proposal also recognizes the significant work and risk undertaken on a contingency basis. Any fee remains subject to court approval, and any portion not awarded should benefit the class.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline is prepared to resolve the case with automatic payments to the identifiable class, but the proposed total exceeds its authorized settlement range. Our counter keeps the process claims-free and makes fees subject to independent court review.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate Brightline's commitment to automatic payments and independent court review. To resolve the case, we propose the following: a $33 million class fund, $8.5 million in attorneys’ fees and expenses subject to court approval, no clear-sailing commitment, and any fee amount not awarded to be added to the class fund. Distribution would remain automatic.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline values the automatic, claims-free distribution and is making a substantial move to reach a court-approvable resolution. We propose a $40 million all-in package, with a $32 million class fund and $8 million in fees and expenses subject to court approval. We will not agree to clear sailing, and any fee amount not awarded will be added to the class fund. Distribution remains automatic.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We accept Brightline’s latest term sheet as binding, subject to court approval.

private_notes.private_reasoning: Open with a firm but negotiable anchor that secures meaningful automatic relief for the class and compensates counsel for substantial contingency work and expenses. Keep any court-disallowed fee with the class rather than allowing it to revert to Brightline.

The proposal must stay below Brightline’s $40 million all-in ceiling while offering a credible, court-approvable settlement. Automatic payments are valuable because the class is fully identifiable. I will counter with a $30 million class fund and $7 million in fees, preserve court review without clear sailing, and have any fees not awarded return to Brightline.

The defense offer provides a meaningful, automatic class recovery, but its fee and reversion terms are unfavorable. Counter with a still-substantial automatic fund and a fee that better reflects the contingency work and invested expenses, while ensuring any fee the court declines goes to class members. Keep the fee subject to court approval and avoid insisting on clear sailing.

Hargrove's proposal exceeds Brightline's $40 million all-in authority. Counter at the authorized ceiling with automatic distribution, no clear sailing, and any fee reduction benefiting the class. This preserves key protections while making a meaningful move from the prior offer.

The latest term provides a substantial $32 million fund with automatic payments, no claims barrier, and any unawarded fee returning to the class. The $8 million fee request is subject to court review, with no clear-sailing commitment. Given trial and certification risks and the strength of the direct class recovery, accepting is preferable to risking the offer in later rounds.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: The settlement was reached through arm’s-length negotiations between class counsel and defense counsel. The negotiations were confidential mediation communications, and this statement does not recount their substance.
